annotation.title_clean: Chapter 837 — Aircraft Operation (Oregon Revised Statutes, 2025 Edition)
annotation.title_en: Chapter 837 — Aircraft Operation (Oregon Revised Statutes, 2025 Edition)
annotation.summary_en: Oregon Revised Statutes Chapter 837 (2025 edition) governing aircraft operation, including a substantial unmanned aircraft systems (drone) part: warrant requirements for law enforcement drone use, public-body drone registration and data policies, bans on weaponized drones, critical-infrastructure overflight offences, civil trespass remedies, and state preemption of local drone regulation.
key_provisions_or_claims: Law enforcement may use drones only with a warrant, consent, exigent circumstances, search and rescue, emergencies or accident reconstruction; unlawfully obtained evidence is inadmissible.
Public bodies must register drones with the Oregon Department of Aviation, report use annually, and publish data retention and sharing policies.

Operating weaponized drones is a misdemeanor or felony, with narrow exceptions requiring FAA authorization, notice, and $1 million liability insurance; projectile drones are banned for crowd management.
Offences for drone overflight of critical infrastructure, harassment over private property, and interference with aircraft or emergency response.
Property owners may sue for treble damages for repeated drone trespass; regulation of drones is preempted from local governments except in local parks.
